newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen up on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen up on Thursday.

text.p: Polish shares eased on Wednesday, falling for the third straight session, but analysts said the market should rebound on Thursday, signalled by stronger buying after price fixing and rises in continuous trade.
Some analysts said, however, that it was possible the market's month-long horizontal trend would continue amid a general lack of positive signals to help spur growth.

"No one doubts there'll be growth tomorrow, the question is whether after the growth there'll be stronger selling after price fixing with people closing positions,", said Pawel Hominski, an analyst at Magnus brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.3 percent to 13,531.0 and turnover fell 9.5 percent to 77.4 million zlotys ($27 million) on both markets. Losers led gainers by 54 to 12 with 17 stocks flat.

Analysts said a good signal was rises in active trade by large-cap stocks such as Wednesday's top gainers, aluminium plant Kety, construction firm Exbud and bank BIG, up 2.5, 1.3 and 1.3 percent respectively.
They said this reflected buying by large investors which could soon help form a growth trend.
But they also said Kety's rise was in part a reaction to an exaggerated low-turnover fall on Tuesday and that some large-cap stocks have fallen of late as well.
Continuous trade turnover was at 3.4 million zlotys ($1.2 million) with five stocks up and three flat.

Mass privatisaton NFI units eased 0.7 percent to 139.5 zlotys ($48.7)in a 13.2-million-zloty ($4.6 million) turnover but rose 2.6 percent to 140.5 zlotys ($49) in 14.5-million- zloty ($5.1 pct) continuous trade.
